title: Walmart, Amazon Face Surprising Shopping Shift
detail:
Walmart, Amazon Face Surprising Shopping Shift

CRM

Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Americans are increasingly using Black Friday discounts to stock up on everyday necessities rather than simply splurging on holiday gifts, signaling a shift in consumer spending that could favor retail giants Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) and Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) while putting pressure on retailers heavily dependent on discretionary purchases.

WMT GF Value chart

Persistent inflation and household budget concerns are changing how Americans approach the holiday shopping season, with artificial intelligence emerging as an increasingly important tool for bargain hunters.

According to Adobe Digital Insights, U.S. consumers spent $82.5 billion online between Nov. 1 and Nov. 22, representing a 9.1% year-over-year increase.

However, the composition of that spending tells a more revealing story.

Online sales of personal hygiene products jumped 40% compared with October's average, while household cleaning products and basic clothing registered increases of 33% and 27%, respectively.

Meanwhile, Salesforce data showed November discounts were 8% deeper than last year, pushing average merchandise selling prices 1% lower.

AI-assisted shopping is also gaining momentum.

Walmart CEO John Furner recently revealed that customers using its AI shopping assistant, Sparky, spent 40% more per order than other shoppers. Amazon CEO Andy Jassy reported that American customers using Alexa spent 50% more than nonusers.

Investors Takeaway

Adobe expects Black Friday online spending to jump 9.2% to $12.9 billion, followed by $15.1 billion on Cyber Monday.

However, strong headline sales may conceal growing pressure on retailer profitability.

Walmart's exposure to essential merchandise could give it a competitive advantage over discretionary-focused retailers such as Target (NYSE:TGT).

Investors should closely monitor merchandise mix, comparable sales, gross margins and inventory levels in upcoming quarterly reports.

Additionally, Walmart and Amazon's AI shopping investments could become meaningful revenue drivers if higher customer spending translates into incremental sales and sustainable profitability rather than simply reflecting the purchasing habits of existing high-spending customers.

title: Wall Street's Insights Into Key Metrics Ahead of Salesforce (CRM) Q3 Earnings

Wall Street's Insights Into Key Metrics Ahead of Salesforce (CRM) Q3 Earnings

The upcoming report from Salesforce (CRM) is expected to reveal quarterly earnings of $3.43 per share, indicating an increase of 5.5% compared to the year-ago period. Analysts forecast revenues of $11.46 billion, representing an increase of 11.7% year over year.

The consensus EPS estimate for the quarter has remained unchanged over the last 30 days. This represents how the covering analysts, as a whole, have reassessed their initial estimates during this timeframe.

Before a company reveals its earnings, it is vital to take into account any changes in earnings projections. These revisions play a pivotal role in predicting the possible reactions of investors toward the stock. Multiple empirical studies have consistently shown a strong association between trends in earnings estimates and the short-term price movements of a stock.

While investors usually depend on consensus earnings and revenue estimates to assess the business performance for the quarter, delving into analysts' forecasts for certain key metrics often provides a more comprehensive understanding.

In light of this perspective, let's dive into the average estimates of certain Salesforce metrics that are commonly tracked and forecasted by Wall Street analysts.

Analysts' assessment points toward 'Revenues- Professional services and other' reaching $515.70 million. The estimate suggests a change of -3.3% year over year.

The average prediction of analysts places 'Revenues- Subscription and support' at $10.95 billion. The estimate indicates a change of +12.6% from the prior-year quarter.

Analysts predict that the 'Revenues- Subscription and support- Agentforce Apps' will reach $7.33 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +219.2%.

The combined assessment of analysts suggests that 'Revenues- Subscription and support- Data 360, Headless Platform, & Other' will likely reach $3.61 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of +65.7%.

The collective assessment of analysts points to an estimated 'Geographic Revenue- Americas' of $8.00 billion. The estimate points to a change of +19.3% from the year-ago quarter.

According to the collective judgment of analysts, 'Geographic Revenue- Asia Pacific' should come in at $1.13 billion. The estimate suggests a change of +4.2% year over year.

Analysts forecast 'Geographic Revenue- Europe' to reach $2.35 billion. The estimate indicates a year-over-year change of -5%.

The consensus estimate for 'Remaining performance obligation (RPO) - Current' stands at $33.46 billion. The estimate is in contrast to the year-ago figure of $29.40 billion.

BR's Sales Backlog & Platform Expansion Fuel Revenue Growth

Broadridge's recurring revenue model, high client retention and expanding product portfolio provide visibility into future growth. Closed sales reached $305 million in fiscal 2026, lifting the backlog to $470 million from $430 million a year earlier. Platform-enabled and next-generation products accounted for nearly 40% of annual closed sales. Growing demand for real-time post-trade solutions, corporate actions and wealth management services supports revenue growth.

The acquisitions of CQG and Kyndryl's Securities Industry Services strengthen its capital markets and Canadian wealth management capabilities, respectively. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, closed sales rose 10% year over year to $36 million, while client retention remained at 98%. Management expects fiscal 2027 closed sales of $290-$330 million, constant-currency recurring revenue growth of 6-8% and adjusted EPS growth of 8-12%.

BR's AI Investments Fuel Revenue & Earnings Growth

Broadridge's investments in agentic Artificial Intelligence (AI) are unlocking new revenue opportunities, accelerating product development and enhancing operational efficiency. Its AI-powered custom policy engine, global demand model and BondGPT are gaining traction. The expansion of its institutional voting solution to global equities and the addition of another Tier 1 wealth management client in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 reflect growing demand. Broadridge has achieved approximately 25% efficiency gains in managed services, with management targeting nearly 50%. The company realized $6 million in AI-driven cost savings in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 and remains on track to achieve $25 million for the full year. These productivity gains should support margin expansion and earnings growth while funding strategic investments.

BR's Strong Cash Flow Sustains Shareholder Returns

Broadridge's recurring revenue model and consistent cash flow generation provide financial flexibility to fund strategic investments and reward shareholders. Free cash flow rose 17% year over year to $1.2 billion in fiscal 2026, with a 110% conversion rate. The company returned more than $1 billion to shareholders through $600 million in share repurchases and $443 million in dividends. It also raised its annual dividend by 12% to $4.36 per share, marking its 20th consecutive annual dividend increase.

title: Salesforce Stock (CRM) Looks Mispriced After the AI Sell-Off
detail:
Salesforce Stock (CRM) Looks Mispriced After the AI Sell-Off

Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Salesforce (CRM) stock looks mispriced after the recent software sell-off, driven by fears that artificial intelligence (AI) will disrupt traditional enterprise software. The customer relationship management software provider enters this stretch from a position of financial strength, having generated $14.4 billion in free cash flow in Fiscal 2026. In the company's second-quarter Fiscal 2027 earnings release in August 2026, Chair and CEO Marc Benioff addressed the AI opportunity and pushed back against the disruption narrative, stating, "AI is delivering value across every layer of our platform."

I think investors are overlooking how little physical investment Salesforce needs to pursue that opportunity, with capex projected at roughly 1.5% of revenue in Fiscal 2027. Rather than being replaced, its software can become more useful and more embedded as enterprises adopt autonomous AI agents across workflows, in my view. Yet the market seems far more concerned about disruption. Ahead of the company's third-quarter earnings report on December 2, I rate CRM a Buy.

AI Exposure Without the Infrastructure Bill

What I like about Salesforce is that it offers AI exposure without the huge infrastructure bill. Now, Monday's rally following Jensen Huang's return to Nvidia (NVDA) lifted CRM 2.7%. Yet shares remain roughly 26% below their August post-earnings level. Investors have sold software alongside companies facing enormous graphics processing unit (GPU) and power commitments, but Salesforce's spending requirements look very different.

For context, Salesforce's Fiscal 2026 operating cash flow reached $15 billion, with FCF of $14.4 billion. However, physical capex consumed only about 4% of operating cash. Its most recent Q2 FY27 results repeated the pattern, with $1.3 billion of operating cash and $1.1 billion of FCF.

We are seeing that Salesforce can keep developing Agentforce without committing tens of billions to new data centers. That leaves more flexibility for shareholder-friendly capital allocation, including ongoing share buybacks and its quarterly dividend. I find that appealing, especially as infrastructure financing has become such a concern elsewhere in the technology sector.

In addition, I have grown fond of AIforce, which also gives Salesforce a sensible response to changing interfaces. Customers can access its data and take governed actions through outside assistants. Following August's Claudeforce integration with Anthropic's (ANT) Claude, Salesforce teamed up with Microsoft (MSFT) last week to launch Copilotforce, bringing Salesforce workflows into Microsoft Copilot (now in public beta) and Teams (currently in pilot).

Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM, XETRA:FOO) remains rated "buy" at Bank of America, which sees a favorable short-term outlook for the stock after a roughly 27% decline from its September peak.

The comapny is set to report its fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on December 2, and the bank is looking for signs of faster organic growth in the second half, momentum in cRPO and bookings, and stronger Agentforce monetization.

Bank of America projects Salesforce's organic revenue growth will rise to 7.4% in the third quarter and 9.9% in the fourth, from 6.4% in the second.

The bank also forecasts third-quarter growth of 13.7% in current remaining performance obligations, or cRPO, on a constant-currency basis.

Autodesk, Inc. ADSK reported third-quarter fiscal 2027 non-GAAP earnings of $3.20 per share, up 19.9% year over year. The figure surpassed the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $3.07 by 4.2%, aided by strong renewal rates, operating leverage and benefits from sales optimization.

Revenues increased 17% year over year to $2.16 billion, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $2.13 billion by 1.4%.

On a constant-currency basis, revenues grew 14%. Strength in construction and emerging markets supported results. Net revenue retention approximated the top end of the 100%-110% range in constant currency.

ADSK's Q3 Top-Line Details

Subscription revenues increased 17.3% year over year to $2.07 billion, while Other revenues rose 1.2% to $87 million. Autodesk reclassified certain consumption-based offerings as subscription revenues, with prior-period figures adjusted accordingly.

Region-wise, Americas revenues increased 18% year over year to $967 million, while EMEA revenues rose 17% to $838 million. APAC revenues advanced 12% to $355 million.

Autodesk, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise
Autodesk, Inc. Price, Consensus and EPS Surprise

Autodesk, Inc. price-consensus-eps-surprise-chart | Autodesk, Inc. Quote

Billings grew 12% year over year to $2.07 billion, or 13% in constant currency. ADSK signed its largest-ever enterprise business agreement (EBA) and completed several EBA renewals during the quarter.

The impact of the sales reorganization continued to diminish across most regions, although Western Europe remained slower to normalize. The new transaction model no longer provided a meaningful benefit to quarterly revenue and billings growth.

Autodesk's Product Portfolio in Detail

Architecture, Engineering and Construction (AEC) revenues increased 19% year over year to $1.10 billion. Construction maintained strong momentum, supported by customers expanding their adoption of Autodesk's connected project workflows.

AutoCAD and AutoCAD LT revenues grew 11% year over year to $525 million. Manufacturing revenues increased 13% to $403 million, with Fusion benefiting from larger deployments and the integration of design and manufacturing workflows.

Other product revenues climbed 35% year over year to $135 million. The newly introduced product family includes Media and Entertainment and Autodesk Operations Solutions.

MaintainX generated nearly $33 million in revenues in its first quarter under Autodesk's ownership, exceeding management's expectations. ADSK plans to expand MaintainX across additional geographies and customer segments in the next fiscal year.
